title: Rain or shine, ASHAs continue their protest seeking better pay

ai.summary: ASHAs in Bengaluru have been protesting for over 10 days demanding ₹15,000 monthly pay instead of current ₹7,000-8,000, citing undervalued work in public healthcare and lack of formal recognition.

facts.quote: an Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) asked, pointing to her son at Freedom Park in Bengaluru, where thousands of frontline workers have been protesting, demanding a monthly payment of ₹15,000.
ASHAs receive around ₹7,000 to ₹8,000 a month, comprising a State government component of around ₹5,000 to ₹6,000 and a fixed Union government incentive of ₹2,000.

facts.claim: ASHAs work more than 2-3 hours a day
facts.quote: Officially, our work is supposed to be for two to three hours, four to five times a week. But in my 10 years as an ASHA, there has not been a day when I have finished within three hours,
We have to collect and handle the samples ourselves. What about our safety?

When the National Rural Health Mission was launched in 2005, ASHAs were described as “community health volunteers” and were expected to contribute one to two hours a day. They say the designation has remained unchanged even as their responsibilities have expanded to cover maternal and child health, immunisation, nutrition support and disease surveillance.

ai.background_note: ASHAs, who are frontline public health workers, have been protesting for better pay and recognition since 2024, with the current protest entering its 10th day in November 2026.
